## Observations

### Simultaneous writers silently lose records, each reporting success

`verified` · `@akr.observation.concurrent-writes-are-silently-lost/1` · scope `path "crates/akr-cli/src/write.rs"`, `path "crates/akr-core/src/ops/**"`

The write pipeline has no cross-process concurrency control for a write that adds a new key, so simultaneous writers clobber one another and every one of them reports success. Six `akr papercut` processes started together against one workspace: all six printed `wrote .akr/records/akr/papercuts.akr` and exited 0, and two records landed. The mechanism is the read-modify-write in crates/akr-core/src/ops: `Staged::load` reads every source, the operation edits the ledger in memory, and `Staged::commit` writes each touched file whole through a temporary and a rename. The rename is atomic per file, which is what docs/07-cli.md section 4 promises, but nothing detects that the file changed between the read and the write, so the last writer's copy — built from a snapshot that predates the others — wins. `base_rev` (docs/08-mcp.md) is optimistic concurrency for `revise`, and guards a same-key conflict only; a new key appended to a shared records file passes no such check. Reproduced identically on the unmodified tree at 968ac27 and on the current working tree, so it is not a consequence of the speed work.

> **Stale** — `watches "crates/akr-core/src/ops/**"` was matched by `f418e73e`, which touched `crates/akr-core/src/ops/exclusion.rs`. See [REVIEW-REQUIRED.md](REVIEW-REQUIRED.md#simultaneous-writers-silently-lose-records-each-reporting-success).

### The 2026-08-25 collated papercuts are seven defects, six stale reports and two correct behaviours

`verified` · `@akr.assessment.papercut-reconciliation-2026-08-25/1` · scope `path "crates/akr-cli/**"`, `path "crates/akr-core/**"`, `path "crates/akr-mcp/**"`, `path "docs/**"`, `path "fixtures/**"`

Reconciliation of @akr.papercut.collated-17-papercuts-from-evidence-intake/1 at
4b3212b16511e2cd2546c26c35271ada3d1cea6a. Every report is disposed of below; nothing

FIXED HERE — SEVEN DEFECTS.

1 V-025 judged every revision rather than the live ones. Superseding a bad evidence
record leaves the offending revision in the file, so the rule survived its own repair
and `knowledge.revise` was refused because the superseded revision still had to
validate; the same reading turned every write in a workspace with a long evidence
history into a refusal carrying ~230 diagnostics about records nobody was touching,
and left a citation whose scratch entry had already been pruned with no repair at all.
Now filtered on `is_live`, as V-023 filters contradictions. This closes three reports:
the evidence-intake circular revise, the jpegXL kept-scratch rejection, and the
SaveYourSkin excluded working ledger. Recorded as the 2026-08-25 amendment to D-037.

2 AKR-T012 refused a word that is no lifecycle state without naming one. `accepted` on
a decision now gets the kind's own states as help. A word that is a real state but
wrong for the kind was already V-007's to refuse and already named the legal set;
that arm is untouched.

3 `get` rendered no acceptance block below `--detail canonical`, so `complete` demanded
mappings the reader had never seen. Both halves now carry each check's statement,
method, command, citations and verdict.

4 `explain <kind>` listed what a kind accepts and never that a planning or empirical
kind rejects `topic`. It now says so, with the code it will be refused under.

5 `budget_tokens` was measured against the records the assembler selected, while the
result carries a rendered text half and a structured duplicate. A caller asking for
4,500 was delivered close to three times that. Assembly now renders, measures both
halves and re-assembles to proportionally less, up to three passes, and every budgeted
bundle reports `requested_tokens` and `delivered_tokens` — plus a note when the
mandatory sections alone exceed the request, which V-123 forbids reducing. It lives in
`akr-cli` so both surfaces keep the promise identically.

6 The pre-commit hook refused a message-only `git commit --amend`, because the change
transaction closes at `akr git commit` and a later commit meets a hook with nothing to
check. `--no-verify` was the only way through. The hook now passes precisely the
reword case: no transaction open, and an index equal to HEAD.

7 A revision reset `last_change` and stranded evidence whose measurement was still
valid, because revision n+1 did not exist before the commit that wrote it. Recorded as
D-038 @akr.decision.revision-is-not-redefinition/1.

ALREADY FIXED, REPORTED FROM STALE SERVER PROCESSES — SIX REPORTS. The generic
`slots` schema, `topic` exposed for every kind, `topic` needing slug syntax, `scope`
advertised as an untyped array, an observation's `method` enum, and an assessment's
required `statement` were all closed on 2026-08-23 by the exact per-kind authoring
schema, and the binaries carrying it were installed the same evening. The six reports

vocabulary version and that did not move.

milestone, work or track is D-009's contract and the error said so. Line citations
requiring a registered source is D-031, the error said so, and the agent's chosen

### The 2026-08-27 collated papercuts are four defects, one spec-correct reset, one remaining deadlock and one environment timeout

`verified` · `@akr.assessment.papercut-reconciliation-2026-08-27/1` · scope `path "crates/akr-cli/**"`, `path "crates/akr-core/**"`, `path "crates/akr-mcp/**"`, `path "docs/07-cli.md"`, `path "fixtures/validate/err/**"`, `path "spec/diagnostics/codes-lang.md"`

Reconciliation of @akr.papercut.collated-7-papercuts-from-lege-ecosystem-jpegxl/1.
Four reports are defects fixed here, one is correct behaviour with a clearer
note, one remains as live work, and one is an environment timeout the CLI
already covers.

FIXED HERE — FOUR DEFECTS.

1 `akr revise --from` with a partial fragment was not a merge. The CLI parsed
the file as a whole record and passed it as `Edits.replace_with`, so any slot
the fragment did not name vanished: slice-8 lost acceptance, phase-4 lost
depends_on/verified_by, Candidate D lost scope/derived_from. `knowledge.revise`
already overlays unmentioned slots (and has tests for it). The CLI now takes
the same merge: named slots replace, including emptying them; the rest of the
head stays. `--from` wrapping uses the head's kind rather than hardcoding
`work`. Documented in docs/07-cli.md and in `akr revise --help`.

2 `akr revise --from` ignored `state` in the body. ops::revise resets a sealed
successor to the class initial state unless `Edits.state` is set, and the CLI
only filled that from `--state`. A body that said `state completed` landed
`proposed`, which is exempt from V-020, so AKR-R022 errors being repaired
vanished for the wrong reason. A `state` slot in the `--from` file now sets
`Edits.state` unless `--state` is also given.

3 AKR-L002 said `{n} revisions are unsuperseded` and pointed at a count.
Revisions written without `supersedes` back-edges are unambiguous only while a
live head exists; the moment a state-only revise makes every revision
terminal, head resolution falls through to the chain-end tier and refuses.
The diagnostic now names the edge-less revisions, and `akr revise` on a new
head adds `supersedes` edges to every same-key revision that lacked one.

4 `knowledge.get` with `detail: canonical` truncated at the tool budget and
the continuation was `detail: summary`, which drops the acceptance block —
the reason an agent asked for canonical. Truncation of a canonical get now
continues at `body`, which still carries each check's statement, method,
command and verified_by.

CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, CLEARER NOTE — ONE REPORT. `akr revise --from` on an
active work head without `--state` creates the successor as `proposed`. That
is docs/07: a content change of sealed knowledge must be accepted again.
@akr.work.revise-lifecycle-semantics/1 already recorded the policy. The write
now prints that the successor starts proposed and that `--state` keeps it
live.

REMAINING — ONE REPORT. Healing an inherited AKR-T023 on evidence that
another record pins by revision still deadlocks: the revise introduces
AKR-L021 on the referrer, D-039 correctly refuses it as new, and the
referrer cannot be moved to n+1 first because n+1 does not exist yet. The
three-write dance (float the pin, revise, re-pin) remains the escape.
Tracked as @akr.work.revise-repoints-pinned-referrers.

ENVIRONMENT — ONE REPORT. The AKR MCP server failing to connect at session
start is a host timeout on stdio handshake, not a ledger diagnostic. The
CLI path (`akr start`, `akr context`, `akr get`) is the supported fallback
and worked. Reinstalling with scripts/setup-akr-mcp.sh is what refreshes a
stale server binary; `skew` cannot catch it because the vocabulary version
did not move.

### The 2026-08-29 AKR papercuts expose three actionable interface defects

`verified` · `@akr.assessment.papercut-reconciliation-2026-08-29/2` · scope `path "crates/akr-cli/**"`, `path "crates/akr-core/src/validate/**"`, `path "crates/akr-mcp/**"`, `path "docs/**"`

Reconciliation found three genuine interface defects. First, the SaveYourSkin report persists on AKR 0.4.0: strict validation promotes a warning to a failing verdict while JSON still labels every diagnostic only by declared severity and text ends with an unexplained `1 error`. Diagnostics now expose `effective_severity`, and text explicitly counts warnings promoted by `--strict`. Second, `akr git commit -m <message>` accepted but ignored the message; it now applies Git-style repeated message paragraphs to the human prose while retaining canonical AKR trailers. This is distinct from the 2026-08-25 amend-hook fix, which already allowed message-only `git commit --amend`. Third, AKR-L031 rejected `work resolves papercut` without naming the valid provenance relation; V-005 now lists source/target-compatible alternatives, including `derived_from`. The focused CLI, core and MCP suites pass.
